route.title: Two side traces, circle powers, and affine radical axes
route.mathematicalIdea: Use the complete proof.md. The side traces X=CL intersect AB and Y=BK intersect AC give c2*t=b2*s from the first angle. The other two angle equalities yield the cyclic or tangent power formulas for circles through C,K,M,X and B,L,N,Y. Compare each circle with the circle through A and the midpoints of BX and CY; the affine power differences vanish on BY and CX, so K and L lie on that circle. Transfer its powers to the supplied circumcenter and use a squared-distance midpoint identity to obtain OM=ON.
orderedMilestones: Extract positive side-trace parameters and prove the exact angle-orientation and noncollinearity facts from the published strict-interior hypotheses.
Derive c2*t=b2*s and the cyclic-or-tangent power values without assuming the trace points avoid the midpoints.
Prove the affine difference of circle powers and the two radical-axis interpolations, placing K and L on the circle through A,S,T.
Transfer the circle to the supplied O and finish by the midpoint squared-distance identity.
assumptionsUsed: Exactly the published hABC, hM, hN, hK, hL, hKangle, hLangle, h1, h2, h3, and hO.
mathematicalRisks: Ordinary angle equalities require explicit orientation or supplementary-angle handling.
X=M and Y=N are not excluded by a generic-position hypothesis; use repeated-root tangent power formulas.
The result concerns every O satisfying IsCircumcentre, not a chosen center.
No unproved geometric helper or published solution.lean may be imported as a certificate.

entries.collectionRationale: A supplied mathematical route replaces initial route generation only; Lean search, independent DAG planning, proof writing, compilation, and integrity gates remain active.
